from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = ["Consider two blocks on a frictionless track.", "One block hits another and a wall.", "We count the total collisions between objects."]
        self.setup_layout("The Setup: A Curious Collision", lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        block1 = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        block2 = Circle(radius=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        wall = Line(start=UP*1.5, end=DOWN*1.5, color=GREY, stroke_width=10)

        self.place_at_grid(block1, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(block2, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(wall, 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.add(block1, block2, wall)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(block1.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(block1.animate.move_to(self.grid['B4']), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(block1.animate.move_to(self.grid['B4'] + LEFT*0.3), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(block1.animate.move_to(self.grid['B4']), run_time=0.2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Phase space motion describes circular arcs.",
            "Projections extract pi digits in base ten.",
            "Mechanics bridges geometry and number theory.",
            "Each collision updates our digital scoreboard.",
            "The unfolding process visualizes pi's sequence."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Unfolding π", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the first few digits of pi on screen
        digits_text = Text("π = 3.1415...", font_size=36, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(digits_text, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(digits_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show collision events incrementing a counter
        counter = Integer(0, font_size=48, color="#FFFF00")
        counter_label = Text("Collisions:", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        VGroup(counter_label, counter).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(counter_label, counter), "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(counter_label), FadeIn(counter))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the counter updating with each collision
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        for i in range(1, 6):
            self.play(counter.animate.set_value(i), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Display the evolving approximation of pi
        pi_approx = Text("Approx: 3.1", font_size=32, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(pi_approx, "F4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(FadeIn(pi_approx))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight the final resulting value of pi
        final_text = Text("π ≈ 3.14159", font_size=40, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "E5", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeOut(digits_text), FadeOut(counter), FadeOut(counter_label), FadeOut(pi_approx), FadeIn(final_text))
        self.play(Circumscribe(final_text, color="#FFFFFF"))

        # --- Animation Content ---

outline.topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digits of π

sections.title: The Setup: A Curious Collision
sections.content: Introduce the physical system: Two blocks of mass m₁ and m₂ on a frictionless track. Block 1 moves towards a stationary Block 2, which is backed by a wall. We count the total number of collisions between the blocks and the wall.
sections.example: Visualize two toy trains: a small train and a massive 'Heavy Hauler' train sitting in front of a giant concrete wall.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly review Elastic Collisions. Use graphical representations: A 2D velocity space (phase space) where the axes are the velocities of the two blocks. The conservation of energy forms an ellipse, and collisions represent 'bounces' along this elliptical path.
sections.example: Show a vector arrow shortening and rotating in phase space, demonstrating how energy is preserved while momentum shifts.

sections.title: The Mass Ratio Connection
sections.content: Explain that the number of collisions is determined by the mass ratio m₂/m₁. As m₂ becomes significantly larger (e.g., m₂ = 100ⁿ * m₁), the sequence of bounces maps onto the digits of π.
sections.example: An animation showing: If m₂ = 100m₁, you get 31 collisions. If m₂ = 10,000m₁, you get 314 collisions, mirroring the digits 3.14.

sections.title: Visualizing the Unfolding π
sections.content: Explain why this happens: The movement in phase space creates an arc of a circle. The projection of this motion effectively performs a base-10 digit extraction of π. This highlights the bridge between classical mechanics and number theory.
sections.example: An animated 'digital scoreboard' above the blocks that clicks up the count of collisions, displaying 3, 1, 4, 1, 5... as the blocks bounce.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Elegance of Mechanics
sections.content: Summarize that the geometry of the collision space is inherently circular, which is why π—the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter—emerges naturally from these linear impacts.
sections.example: A final visual overlay of a circle traced over the phase space trajectory, showing the blocks 'bouncing' around the circumference of π.
